recent_posts.title: Introducing Akka Specify
recent_posts.summary: Akka has launched Akka Specify, a new feature enabling spec-driven development (SDD) for building agentic AI systems without manual coding or an IDE. It integrates with popular AI coding assistants like Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and Codex via slash commands. The workflow follows a structured loop: specify requirements, clarify gaps, plan implementation, generate tasks, and implement code. Akka extends this with utilities for local builds, testing, cluster execution, security scans, and deployment to Akka Automated Operations. The tool is based on the spec-kit SDD framework and aims to reduce the journey from idea to production to hours.

recent_posts.title: Manulife Selects Akka to Operationalize Agentic AI within its Enterprise AI Platform
recent_posts.summary: Manulife has selected Akka as a foundational platform for its enterprise agentic AI initiative. Akka's durable, highly available runtime will provide the security, reliability, and scalability needed to deploy AI agents across critical business workflows in a regulated environment. Manulife's enterprise AI platform, currently in beta, aims to embed AI across the organization with strong governance and Responsible AI practices. The company expects AI to generate over $1 billion in enterprise value by 2027, with roughly one-fifth from efficiency gains. Manulife was previously ranked the #1 life insurance company for AI maturity in the Evident AI Index.

recent_posts.title: What is Agentic AI?
recent_posts.summary: Agentic AI involves autonomous systems that use LLMs to make decisions and take actions, but moving from prototype to production requires addressing significant risks. These risks span both traditional distributed systems challenges and the non-deterministic nature of LLMs. Production readiness depends on establishing trust through thorough risk management rather than perfect results. The complexity goes far beyond simple prompt-based agents talking to LLMs.

recent_posts.title: How Akka resolves split brain conflicts in distributed systems
recent_posts.summary: Akka handles split-brain scenarios in distributed systems through event sourcing and version vectors, enabling fine-grained conflict resolution at the entity level. When a region fails during multi-region deployment, the system preserves all events in immutable journals, allowing deterministic merge operations that favor the surviving region's timeline while maintaining a complete audit trail. This approach avoids traditional disaster recovery pitfalls like point-in-time rollbacks that affect unrelated data, instead resolving conflicts only for affected entities while keeping discarded events available for compensating actions.

recent_posts.title: Trustworthy AI with Akka
recent_posts.summary: Akka's architecture enables trustworthy AI through built-in transparency, accountability, privacy protection, and safety mechanisms. The platform provides immutable audit trails, cryptographic signing, end-to-end encryption, and Zero Trust principles. Organizations must actively implement input validation, least privilege access, human-in-the-loop controls, and continuous monitoring to build truly trustworthy AI systems. Akka aims for "continuous compliance" with emerging standards like ISO/IEC 42001 and NIST AI Risk Management Framework.

recent_posts.title: Why most agentic AI projects fail and what production experience teaches us
recent_posts.summary: Agentic AI systems are fundamentally distributed systems that require production-hardened infrastructure to succeed. While the market shows significant hype with high valuations and low revenue multiples, 95% of AI projects are failing due to infrastructure engineering challenges rather than lack of imagination. These systems introduce new complexity layers including stochastic components, specialized GPU infrastructure, long-lived workflows, and side-effecting actions. Building reliable agentic systems requires experience with durability, observability, backpressure, and fault tolerance - lessons learned from 15 years of distributed systems development at scale.

recent_posts.title: News: Akka and Deloitte Canada Collaborate to Deliver Agentic AI at Scale
recent_posts.summary: Akka and Deloitte Canada have partnered to address enterprise challenges in deploying agentic AI systems at scale. The collaboration leverages Akka's platform, which has been downloaded over 1 billion times and is used by companies like Capital One and Walmart, to solve critical issues around cost, performance, and resilience in mission-critical AI deployments. Agentic AI requires a shift from transaction-centered to conversation-centered architectures, maintaining state within services rather than relying on traditional stateless CRUD operations. The Akka Agentic Platform promises 3X development velocity with 1/3 the compute resources, featuring orchestration, durable memory, event-driven systems capable of 10 million TPS, and multi-region deployment capabilities.

recent_posts.title: Agentic Systems Are Distributed Systems
recent_posts.summary: Enterprise agentic AI systems inherently require distributed system architectures to handle production challenges like distributed memory, streaming I/O with LLMs, stateful orchestration, semantic search, and resilient deployment across clusters. Key requirements include managing conversation history across nodes, handling LLM streaming failures and network partitions, orchestrating multi-agent workflows, integrating with vector databases for RAG, and ensuring fault tolerance across regions. Building production-ready agentic systems demands robust distributed systems frameworks rather than simple demo-style monolithic approaches.

recent_posts.title: Event Sourcing: The Backbone of Agentic AI
recent_posts.summary: Event sourcing provides the ideal foundation for building agentic AI systems by offering perfect recall, auditability, and support for distributed agent communication. The pattern naturally handles the demanding requirements of AI agents including memory storage, context retrieval, asynchronous streaming, and nondeterministic behavior evaluation. Key concepts covered include prompt engineering as critical for success, retrieval augmented generation for knowledge enhancement, and how event sourcing enables fearless experimentation and multi-agent coordination through immutable event logs.

recent_posts.title: Beyond the Hype: How to address AI agent dev framework obstacles
recent_posts.summary: Gartner identifies AI agent development frameworks as transformational but warns of key obstacles including framework immaturity, lack of built-in guardrails, Python-centric limitations, nondeterministic behavior risks, complex multi-agent orchestration, and amplified inference costs. Akka addresses these challenges through its mature 15-year platform offering backwards compatibility, built-in evaluation and safety mechanisms, JVM-native enterprise integration, human-in-the-loop workflows, event-driven multi-agent orchestration, and cost optimization features including context compaction and flexible model routing.
